knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral Expression For the Arc Length of a Curve

question.:question/problem:
![](images/0e/0e3f80c8a0975c70ee2990dc230af59ffb9f0944bdbdc86c6fb96f693ebdac29.png)

Which integral  expression gives the arc length of the curve $h(t)=(2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)})\,i+(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)})\,j+(3 t)\,k$ from $t=0$ to $t=2 \pi?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $h'(t)$ and $\|h'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}h'(t) & =(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}))\,i+(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)}))\,j+(\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 t))\,k \\  & =(- 4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)})\,i+(4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)})\,j+(3)\,k \\ \|h'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(- 4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + 3^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16 \sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + 16 \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + 9} \\  & =\sqrt{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is:

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\|h'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t=\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\sqrt{25}\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral Expression For the Arc Length of a Curve

question.:question/problem: Which integral expression gives the arc length of the curve $f(t)=\langle 2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\,3 e^{2 t},\,2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\rangle$ from $t=-1$ to $t=1?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $f'(t)$ and $\|f'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 e^{2 t}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)})\rangle \\  & =\langle - 4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\,6 e^{2 t},\,4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\rangle \\ \|f'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(- 4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(4 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 4 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(6 e^{2 t}\right)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(16 \sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} - 32 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} \cos{\left(2 t \right)} + 16 \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)}\right) + \left(16 \sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + 32 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} \cos{\left(2 t \right)} + 16 \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)}\right) + 36 e^{4 t}} \\  & =\sqrt{32 \left(\sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)}\right) + 36 e^{4 t}} \\  & =\sqrt{36 e^{4 t} + 32}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{-1}^{1}\|f'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_{-1}^{1}2 \sqrt{9 e^{4 t} + 8}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{\left(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} + 9 e^{4 t}}\,\mathrm{d}t

question.:question/problem:
![](images/35/3500678bdca0125f1796c68ad54aab04c05ece23914f2bde0a0589119d291fc8.png)

Which integral  expression gives the arc length of the curve $g(t)=\langle 4 t \sin{\left(t \right)},\,- 4 t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2\rangle$
from  $t=0$ to $t=\pi?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $g'(t)$ and $\|g'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}g'(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4 t \sin{\left(t \right)}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(- 4 t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2)\rangle \\  & =\langle 4 t \cos{\left(t \right)} + 4 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,4 t \sin{\left(t \right)} - 4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle \\ \|g'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(4 t \sin{\left(t \right)} - 4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(4 t \cos{\left(t \right)} + 4 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(16 t^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 32 t \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 16 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right) + \left(16 t^{2} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 32 t \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 16 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)} \\  & =\sqrt{16 t^{2} + 16}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is:

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{0}^{\pi}\|g'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t=\int_{0}^{\pi}4 \sqrt{t^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Which integral expression gives the arc length of the curve $f(t)=\langle \sin{\left(3 t \right)} + \cos{\left(3 t \right)},\,4 e^{2 t},\,\sin{\left(3 t \right)} - \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\rangle$ from $t=-1$ to $t=1?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $f'(t)$ and $\|f'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f'(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\sin{\left(3 t \right)} + \cos{\left(3 t \right)}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4 e^{2 t}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\sin{\left(3 t \right)} - \cos{\left(3 t \right)})\rangle \\  & =\langle - 3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(3 t \right)},\,8 e^{2 t},\,3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\rangle \\ \|f'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(- 3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(8 e^{2 t}\right)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(9 \sin^{2}{\left(3 t \right)} - 18 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} \cos{\left(3 t \right)} + 9 \cos^{2}{\left(3 t \right)}\right) + \left(9 \sin^{2}{\left(3 t \right)} + 18 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} \cos{\left(3 t \right)} + 9 \cos^{2}{\left(3 t \right)}\right) + 64 e^{4 t}} \\  & =\sqrt{18 \left(\sin^{2}{\left(3 t \right)} + \cos^{2}{\left(3 t \right)}\right) + 64 e^{4 t}} \\  & =\sqrt{64 e^{4 t} + 18}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{-1}^{1}\|f'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{2} \sqrt{32 e^{4 t} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{\left(\sin{\left(3 t \right)} - \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right)^{2} + \left(\sin{\left(3 t \right)} + \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right)^{2} + 16 e^{4 t}}\,\mathrm{d}t

question.:question/problem: Which integral expression gives the arc length of the curve $r(t)=\langle \left(\sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t},\,2 t e^{2 t},\,\left(3 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t}\rangle$ from $t=0$ to $t=1?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\left(\sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 t e^{2 t}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\left(3 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t})\rangle \\  & =\langle \left(- 6 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t} + 2 \left(\sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t},\,4 t e^{2 t} + 2 e^{2 t},\,\left(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 6 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t} + 2 \left(3 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t}\rangle \\ \|r'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(4 t e^{2 t} + 2 e^{2 t}\right)^{2} + \left(\left(- 6 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t} + 2 \left(\sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t}\right)^{2} + \left(\left(2 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 6 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t} + 2 \left(3 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t}\right)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(16 t^{2} e^{4 t} + 16 t e^{4 t} + 4 e^{4 t}\right) + \left(16 e^{4 t} \sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} - 64 e^{4 t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} \cos{\left(2 t \right)} + 64 e^{4 t} \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)}\right) + \left(64 e^{4 t} \sin^{2}{\left(2 t \right)} + 64 e^{4 t} \sin{\left(2 t \right)} \cos{\left(2 t \right)} + 16 e^{4 t} \cos^{2}{\left(2 t \right)}\right)} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(4 \left(2 t + 1\right)^{2} + 80\right) e^{4 t}} \\  & =\sqrt{4 \left(2 t + 1\right)^{2} + 80} e^{2 t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{0}^{1}\|r'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_{0}^{1}2 \sqrt{\left(2 t + 1\right)^{2} + 20} e^{2 t}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{4 t^{2} e^{4 t} + \left(\sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} e^{4 t} + \left(3 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} - \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^{2} e^{4 t}}\,\mathrm{d}t

\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{\left(4 t e^{2 t} + 2 e^{2 t}\right)^{2} + \left(\left(- 6 \sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t} + 2 \left(\sin{\left(2 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right) e^{2 t}\right)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}t

question.:question/problem: Which integral expression gives the arc length of the curve $r(t)=\langle \left(\sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t},\,t e^{t},\,\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t}\rangle$ from $t=0$ to $t=1?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find $r'(t)$ and $\|r'(t)\|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r'(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\left(\sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t e^{t}),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t})\rangle \\  & =\langle \left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t} + \left(\sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t},\,t e^{t} + e^{t},\,\left(\sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t} + \left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t}\rangle \\ \|r'(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(t e^{t} + e^{t}\right)^{2} + \left(\left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t} + \left(\sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t}\right)^{2} + \left(\left(\sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t} + \left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) e^{t}\right)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(t^{2} e^{2 t} + 2 t e^{2 t} + e^{2 t}\right) + \left(e^{2 t} \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 6 e^{2 t} \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 9 e^{2 t} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right) + \left(9 e^{2 t} \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 6 e^{2 t} \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + e^{2 t} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(\left(t + 1\right)^{2} + 10\right) e^{2 t}} \\  & =\sqrt{\left(t + 1\right)^{2} + 10} e^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{0}^{1}\|r'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{\left(t + 1\right)^{2} + 10} e^{t}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{t^{2} e^{2 t} + \left(\sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)^{2} e^{2 t} + \left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)^{2} e^{2 t}}\,\mathrm{d}t
\int_{0}^{1}t^{2} e^{2 t} + 2 t e^{2 t} + 10 e^{2 t} \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 10 e^{2 t} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + e^{2 t}\,\mathrm{d}t

question.:question/problem: Which integral expression gives the arc length of the curve $r(t)=\langle \left(\sin{\left(3 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right) e^{3 t},\,3 t e^{3 t},\,\left(3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} - \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right) e^{3 t}\rangle$ from $t=0$ to $t=1?$

$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =\int_{0}^{1}\|r'(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_{0}^{1}3 \sqrt{\left(3 t + 1\right)^{2} + 20} e^{3 t}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{9 t^{2} e^{6 t} + \left(\sin{\left(3 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right)^{2} e^{6 t} + \left(3 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} - \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right)^{2} e^{6 t}}\,\mathrm{d}t

\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{\left(9 t e^{3 t} + 3 e^{3 t}\right)^{2} + \left(\left(- 9 \sin{\left(3 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right) e^{3 t} + 3 \left(\sin{\left(3 t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(3 t \right)}\right) e^{3 t}\right)^{2}}\,\mathrm{d}t
